UnitStatement: The integration plan identifies concrete changes needed to integrate OpenPipeStress with the Chirality App agent framework.
The preferred integration is a filesystem-native, deterministic domain-tool integration.
Chirality should not embed the OpenPipeStress GUI, solver, or model engine.
OpenPipeStress should not become a general-purpose agent operating system.
Chirality App orchestrates agents, deliverables, review notes, change records, dependency registers, summaries, and human gates.
OpenPipeStress owns the physical piping model, analytical model, solver, model states, analysis runs, comparisons, handoff packages, and GUI editing.
The OpenPipeStress Tool Adapter exposes deterministic commands that Chirality can call safely.
The human operator accepts or rejects changes and decides what can be relied upon.
The integration should give Chirality visibility into OpenPipeStress work without letting agents directly mutate engineering model truth.
Integration should proceed through levels rather than jumping directly to deep automation.
Level 0 requires no code integration.
At Level 0, the user runs OpenPipeStress manually.
At Level 0, the user exports summaries, reports, manifests, and comparison files.
At Level 0, Chirality agents read exported files and help with review notes, assumptions, TBDs, handoff checklists, and deliverable scaffolding.
At Level 1, Chirality can call OpenPipeStress tools that do not mutate canonical model truth.
Level 1 example commands include model validation, model summarization, state listing, run listing, comparison listing, private-data boundary checks, and professional-boundary language checks.
At Level 2, Chirality can request OpenPipeStress to produce analysis runs, comparisons, and handoff packages through the adapter.
Level 2 generated outputs are domain-controlled writes rather than raw agent writes.
Level 2 example commands include running analysis, comparing states, comparing runs, generating handoff packages, and generating report fragments.
Some domain-controlled output generation commands should require explicit user confirmation.
At Level 3, agents can create structured operation proposals.
At Level 3, OpenPipeStress validates and previews structured operation proposals.
At Level 3, the user accepts or rejects proposals in the OpenPipeStress GUI or through a future deterministic approval path.
The Level 3 proposal workflow validates an agent proposal, routes the diff to user review, applies through OpenPipeStress, and creates a new model state.
Level 4 external result state support is future-only.
At Level 4, users may import or manually enter selected external professional-tool results as structured result states.
At Level 4, OpenPipeStress compares external result states using its generic comparison engine.
At Level 4, Chirality summarizes comparison results but does not declare validation or professional acceptance.
The target architecture places Chirality Desktop Harness above deterministic tool calls to the OpenPipeStress Tool Adapter or CLI.
The Chirality Desktop Harness contains agents, workbench or pipeline surfaces, deliverables, dependency registers, lifecycle records, and git-tracked project truth.
Chirality and the OpenPipeStress adapter exchange deterministic tool calls, manifests, proposals, and summaries.

The OpenPipeStress Tool Adapter or CLI validates schema, summarizes models, lists states and runs, runs analysis, compares states or runs, generates handoff packages and report fragments, and validates operation proposals.
The OpenPipeStress domain application contains the 3D GUI, schema-backed physical model, analytical model, solver, model states, analysis runs, comparison records, and handoff packages.
Chirality-side integration artifacts include the PRD amendment, domain engine profile specification, domain tool adapter specification, write-boundary policy, and operation proposal specification.
OpenPipeStress-side integration artifacts include the Chirality profile, artifact layout, CLI adapter spec, operation proposal schema, report fragment spec, and handoff manifest spec.
A real project should include model manifests, warnings, assumptions, run summaries, comparison summaries, delta tables, handoff manifests, export warnings, TBD registers, and review notes.
The recommended project layout centers OpenPipeStress work in the piping design package under a dedicated OpenPipeStress model deliverable.
The design-basis deliverable contains status, datasheet, specification, guidance, procedure, and TBD register files.
The OpenPipeStress model deliverable contains status, model manifests, warnings, assumptions, and OpenPipeStress project folders for states, runs, comparisons, handoff, and proposals.
The internal stress analysis deliverable stores run summaries and solver diagnostics.
The state comparison deliverable stores comparison summary, delta table, and review notes.
The external prover handoff deliverable stores handoff manifest, export warnings, and external review TBDs.
Project sources include line lists, P&ID extracts, equipment interfaces, and owner requirements.
The recommended project layout includes reconciliation space for piping model reconciliation and change space for model change records.
The OpenPipeStress adapter should expose commands with strict input and output schemas.
ops.validate_model validates schema, units, topology, missing inputs, private-data references, and solve blockers.
ops.validate_model accepts a model_path and optional state_id input.
ops.validate_model outputs validation summary JSON, validation summary Markdown, warnings, and blockers.
ops.summarize_model generates a Chirality-readable model summary.
ops.summarize_model outputs Model_Manifest.yaml, Model_Manifest.md, Model_Warnings.md, and Model_Assumptions.md.
ops.list_states lists available model states.
ops.list_states outputs states_index.yaml and states_index.md.
ops.list_runs lists available analysis runs.
ops.list_runs outputs runs_index.yaml and runs_index.md.
ops.run_analysis runs internal OpenPipeStress analysis on a selected model state.
ops.run_analysis accepts model_state_id, analysis_settings_id, load_cases, and optional approval_ref inputs.
ops.run_analysis outputs an analysis run directory containing analysis_run.yaml, results_summary.md, solver_diagnostics.md, and warnings.md.
ops.run_analysis is a domain-controlled write.
ops.run_analysis should not mutate the model state.
ops.run_analysis may require explicit user confirmation in Chirality depending on profile settings.
ops.compare_states compares two model states.
ops.compare_states accepts model_state_a, model_state_b, optional mapping_table, and tolerance_profile inputs.
ops.compare_states outputs comparison.yaml, comparison_summary.md, changed_entities.csv, and unmatched_entities.csv.
ops.compare_runs compares two analysis runs.
ops.compare_runs accepts analysis_run_a, analysis_run_b, mapping_table, and tolerance_profile inputs.
ops.compare_runs outputs comparison.yaml, result_delta_table.csv, comparison_summary.md, and out_of_tolerance.md.
ops.generate_handoff generates a handoff package for downstream modeling or external professional stress-analysis validation.
ops.generate_handoff outputs handoff manifest files, exported model file, units manifest, entity ID manifest, warnings, and unresolved assumptions.
ops.generate_handoff is a domain-controlled write.
ops.generate_handoff should require explicit user confirmation before generation or final packaging.
ops.generate_report_fragment produces report sections that Chirality may include in a larger deliverable package.
ops.generate_report_fragment outputs analysis summary, warnings and assumptions, comparison summary, and professional boundary notice fragments.
ops.validate_operation_proposal validates a proposed model operation without applying it.
ops.validate_operation_proposal accepts proposal_path and base_model_state inputs.
ops.validate_operation_proposal outputs proposal validation files, proposal diff preview, blockers, and warnings.
ops.apply_operation_proposal is future-only.
ops.apply_operation_proposal applies a validated proposal through OpenPipeStress with explicit human approval.
ops.apply_operation_proposal accepts proposal_path, base_model_state, and approval_ref inputs.
ops.apply_operation_proposal outputs a new model state ID, operation_application_record.yaml, and operation_application_record.md.
ops.apply_operation_proposal must never be implemented as raw file mutation by an agent.
ops.apply_operation_proposal must go through OpenPipeStress validation and state creation.
A minimal OpenPipeStress operation proposal includes schema version, id, title, creator, creation timestamp, and base model state.
An operation proposal operation block describes the operation type, target line, proposed location, and support type.
An operation proposal rationale includes a summary and evidence references such as analysis runs and comparisons.
An operation proposal records considered constraints such as rack support zones and clearance zones.
An operation proposal records unresolved assumptions such as pending structural attachment details and guide stiffness confirmation.
An operation proposal professional boundary can mark the proposal as proposal_only.
An operation proposal notice can state that the proposal is not an accepted engineering change until reviewed and applied by the user through OpenPipeStress.
The model review workflow starts with the agent calling ops.summarize_model.
In the model review workflow, the agent reads Model_Manifest.md, warnings, and assumptions.
In the model review workflow, the agent updates the TBD register and drafts review notes.
In the model review workflow, the user reviews notes and decides actions.
The analysis review workflow starts when the user or agent requests ops.run_analysis.
In the analysis review workflow, OpenPipeStress creates an analysis run.
In the analysis review workflow, the agent summarizes solver diagnostics and warnings and drafts analysis review notes.
In the analysis review workflow, the human user evaluates engineering significance.
The comparison workflow starts with the user selecting State or Run A and State or Run B.
In the comparison workflow, Chirality calls ops.compare_states or ops.compare_runs.
In the comparison workflow, OpenPipeStress produces comparison records and delta tables.
In the comparison workflow, the agent summarizes major deltas, unresolved issues, and suggested review questions.
In the comparison workflow, the user decides whether to modify the model.
The external prover feedback workflow starts with the user validating or reviewing the model in external professional stress software.
In the external prover feedback workflow, the user records external review comments manually in Chirality or OpenPipeStress.
In the external prover feedback workflow, the agent turns comments into TBDs or operation proposals.
In the external prover feedback workflow, the user applies changes through OpenPipeStress, saves a new model state, reruns internal analysis, and compares old and new states or runs.
The handoff package workflow starts when the user requests a handoff package.
In the handoff package workflow, Chirality calls ops.generate_handoff.
In the handoff package workflow, OpenPipeStress generates the handoff manifest and export files.
In the handoff package workflow, the agent drafts a handoff checklist and export warnings summary.
In the handoff package workflow, the user transfers the package to the downstream modeling or prover workflow.
Agents may write only in permitted paths.
Agent-writable content includes operation proposals, review notes, TBD registers, draft report sections, handoff checklists, dependency entries, change records, and reconciliation notes.

Agents must not directly write OpenPipeStress project.ops.yaml, accepted model states, analysis run result files, comparison result files, handoff internals, solver outputs, professional acceptance records, private rule packs, private component libraries, or private material libraries.
Domain tools may write only through declared domain-controlled operations.
Domain-controlled operations may write analysis runs, comparison records, handoff packages, report fragments, validation summaries, and manifest outputs.

Human review is required for accepted model changes, external prover interpretation, professional reliance, final report issuance, code-compliance conclusions, construction, fabrication, operation decisions, and private data release.
EP-C-DOM-001 implements a schema for domain profiles.
EP-C-DOM-001 deliverables include DOMAIN_ENGINE_PROFILE_SPEC.md, a profile validation tool, an OpenPipeStress example profile, and tests for invalid profiles.
EP-C-DOM-002 extends or wraps the deterministic tool registry for domain-engine tools.
EP-C-DOM-002 deliverables include domain tool registration, argument schemas, output schemas, invocation API, and execution logging.
EP-C-DOM-003 adds guardrails for protected domain paths.
EP-C-DOM-003 deliverables include protected path matching, agent-writable path matching, write-attempt validation, error messages, and test fixtures.
EP-C-DOM-004 scans working roots for domain artifacts.
EP-C-DOM-004 deliverables include a domain artifact index, profile status summary, model/run/comparison/handoff discovery, and UI read-only display.
EP-C-DOM-005 allows agents to create and validate operation proposals.
EP-C-DOM-005 deliverables include proposal templates, proposal schema validation, proposal browser, validation tool invocation, and review-note linkage.
EP-C-DOM-006 supports domain-specific report fragments and professional/IP boundary checks.
EP-C-DOM-006 deliverables include report fragment ingestion, professional boundary checker, private data leakage checker, and protected-content warning workflow.
EP-OPS-CHIR-001 creates an OpenPipeStress CLI adapter with stable commands.

EP-OPS-CHIR-001 deliverables include validate-model, summarize-model, list-states, list-runs, run-analysis, compare-states, compare-runs, generate-handoff, generate-report-fragment, and validate-operation-proposal commands.
EP-OPS-CHIR-002 defines where generated summaries, manifests, reports, warnings, and proposals live.
EP-OPS-CHIR-002 deliverables include the artifact layout specification, sample project root, sample model manifest, sample run summary, and sample comparison summary.
EP-OPS-CHIR-003 generates bounded outputs for agents.
EP-OPS-CHIR-003 deliverables include model manifests, run summaries, comparison summaries, handoff manifests, warnings, and assumptions.
EP-OPS-CHIR-004 defines structured model operation proposal formats.
EP-OPS-CHIR-004 deliverables include an operation proposal schema, proposal examples, validation command, and diff preview command.
EP-OPS-CHIR-005 is future work for human-gated proposal application.
EP-OPS-CHIR-005 deliverables include proposal review UI, apply operation command, approval reference capture, new model state creation, and operation application record.
EP-OPS-CHIR-006 creates deterministic checks for generated outputs.
EP-OPS-CHIR-006 deliverables include professional-boundary language checking, private-data leakage checking, protected-content risk checking, and report notice generation.

Chirality tests should cover domain profile validation, protected path matching, agent-writable path matching, domain artifact scanning, tool invocation argument validation, tool output capture, failed tool behavior, proposal file validation, and prevention of direct protected-path writes.

OpenPipeStress tests should cover CLI success and failure paths, schema validation outputs, deterministic model summaries, deterministic state/run listings, analysis reproducibility, deterministic comparisons, handoff manifest completeness, proposal validation without mutation, private-data redaction, and professional-boundary notices.
End-to-end tests should create a fixture project at fixture_projects/open_pipe_stress_chirality_demo/.

The end-to-end test flow validates domain profile discovery, model summarization, manifest review, review-note drafting, analysis run creation, comparison delta creation, comparison summary drafting, handoff generation, and protected-path verification.
Implementation Phase 0 is owned by product or architecture.
Phase 0 deliverables include the PRD amendment, DOMAIN_ENGINE_PROFILE_SPEC.md, OPENPIPESTRESS_CHIRALITY_PROFILE.yaml, and OPENPIPESTRESS_CLI_ADAPTER_SPEC.md.
Phase 0 exits when domain engine integration is formally scoped, the OpenPipeStress profile is drafted, and protected and agent-writable paths are defined.
Implementation Phase 1 is owned by OpenPipeStress development.
Phase 1 deliverables include ops.validate_model, ops.summarize_model, ops.list_states, and ops.list_runs.
Phase 1 exits when Chirality can read model summaries without mutating model truth.
Implementation Phase 2 is owned by Chirality development.
Phase 2 deliverables include a profile loader, profile validator, artifact scanner, tool registry entries, and protected path guard.
Phase 2 exits when Chirality can discover an OpenPipeStress project and list safe artifacts and tools.
Implementation Phase 3 is shared.
Phase 3 deliverables include ops.run_analysis, ops.compare_states, ops.compare_runs, ops.generate_handoff, domain tool invocation UI/API, and tool output capture.
Phase 3 exits when the user can trigger deterministic OpenPipeStress outputs from Chirality without direct agent writes to canonical model truth.
Implementation Phase 4 is shared.
Phase 4 deliverables include operation proposal templates, proposal validation, proposal browser, and review notes linkage.
Phase 4 exits when agents can propose model changes as files, OpenPipeStress can validate proposals, and the user remains the application and acceptance gate.
Implementation Phase 5 is shared.
Phase 5 deliverables include deep links to open models, states, runs, comparisons, and proposals in OpenPipeStress.
Phase 5 exits when the user can move from Chirality review context into the OpenPipeStress GUI quickly.
Implementation Phase 6 is owned by OpenPipeStress first and Chirality second.
Phase 6 deliverables include external result state schema, manual external result entry or import, comparison support, and Chirality summary generation.
Phase 6 exits when the user can compare internal OpenPipeStress results against structured external result states without Chirality declaring professional validation.
Immediate next actions start by adding the Chirality PRD amendment to project documentation.
Immediate next actions include drafting DOMAIN_ENGINE_PROFILE_SPEC.md, OPENPIPESTRESS_CHIRALITY_PROFILE.yaml, and OPENPIPESTRESS_CLI_ADAPTER_SPEC.md.
Immediate next actions implement read-only OpenPipeStress adapter commands first.
Immediate next actions implement Chirality profile validation and artifact scanning second.
Analysis, comparison, and handoff tool invocation should be added only after read-only adapter commands, profile validation, and artifact scanning.
Raw external prover parsing, formal prover status, and automatic approval workflows should be deferred.
A successful first integration begins with selecting a Chirality working root and detecting an OpenPipeStress project.
In a successful first integration, an agent reviews the piping model state by calling deterministic OpenPipeStress summary tools.
In a successful first integration, the agent drafts review notes and TBDs from actual model warnings.
In a successful first integration, the user runs or selects an analysis run and the agent summarizes solver diagnostics and changed results.
In a successful first integration, the user requests a handoff package, OpenPipeStress generates it, and Chirality creates the handoff checklist and deliverable record.
In a successful first integration, the human user decides what to do next.
No agent fabricates engineering results.
No agent directly edits canonical model truth.
No software claims professional approval.
The project record remains local, versioned, inspectable, and governed.
Chirality should govern the work around OpenPipeStress.
OpenPipeStress should perform and preserve the engineering model and analysis.
The external professional tool should be used for relied-upon validation.
Human judgment should be used for acceptance.
